The main takeaway from our work is that
the total variation in MDPs is a useful quantity to characterize the regret in the non-stationary setting.
the regret bound depends on the total variation in MDPs rather than the total variation in reward functions or state-transition probabilities.
the regret bound for reinforcement learning in MDPs with non-stationary dynamics and rewards is not necessarily worse than the regret bound for the stationary case.
